evidence.quote: For DNA tasks, we use Evo2-1B, a genome foundation model trained for genome-scale sequence modeling and design across domains of life [38].
For the post-CPT SFT and RL stages we couple the text backbone to a frozen Evo2-1B encoder via a trainable linear projection [38];
For RNA and transcriptomic tasks, we use TranscriptFormer, a cross-species single-cell model trained over evolutionary-scale transcriptomic data [45].
For the downstream SFT and RL stages, we couple the text backbone to a frozen TranscriptFormer encoder through a trainable linear projection [45].
For protein tasks, we use ESM-3, a protein language model trained to model sequence, structure, and function across evolutionary scales [52].
The text backbone is paired with a frozen ESM-3 small protein encoder [52].
For the post-CPT SFT and RL stages we couple the text backbone to a frozen Evo2-1B encoder via a trainable linear projection [38];
For the downstream SFT and RL stages, we couple the text backbone to a frozen TranscriptFormer encoder through a trainable linear projection [45].

Per-residue embeddings are extracted from layer 37 of ESM-3, projected through a trainable linear layer into the text-embedding space, and inserted at the protein placeholder positions before the text tokens [52].

evidence.quote: In our benchmark, we remove this GO graph input and treat the task as reasoning from protein representations plus textual biological metadata alone.

This simplification preserves the core challenge of integrating sequence-derived and symbolic evidence for protein function prediction, while making the protein task architecturally comparable to the DNA and RNA settings studied in the main text.
